articleTitle: A Novel Configurable High-precision and Low-cost Circuit Design of Sigmoid and Tanh Activation Function
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a configurable Sigmoid and Tanh activation function circuit design by second-order approximation and deviation compensation. The proposed circuit is synthesized in TSMC 180nm technology within a 7218 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area at 500MHz, it is also deployed on Xilinx ZC706 FPGA by 158 LUTs and 46 FFs at 333MHz. It achieves almost 4.68× better precision and 20.2% less area than previous works. The experimental results show that our method has almost no accuracy loss on LSTM Chinese speech recognition tasks and the YOLOv3 image recognition post-processing task.

articleTitle: Hardware Resource and Computational Density Efficient CNN Accelerator Design Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become more and more popular in machine vision tasks, including image classification and object detection. As one of the most promising platforms for accelerating CNNs, Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) can achieve a better trade-off between speed, flexibility, cost, and power consumption, thus is more suitable in Edge-AI scenarios, which is generally constrained by cost and power. In this paper, by flexibly using line buffer and tiling, we propose an efficient CNN accelerator design based on FPGA. The implementation results indicate the peak performance of the proposed accelerator can reach 172.8 GOP/s, only occupying 24K LUTs (Look-Up-Table), 40.5 BRAMs (Block Ram), and 296 DSP48s, which shows the highest efficiency of hardware resource and computational density compared with previous works.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band CMOS Switched-Type Phase Shifter with Low Gain Error
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Ka-band 5-bit switched-type phase shifter (STPS) with 180° phase shift range. Optimizations of the phase shift units are performed to achieve wideband phase shift operation and reduce the gain error among the phase states. Implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology, the proposed 5-bit STPS achieves a measured RMS phase error of < 3.6° across 26-30 GHz. The gain error among the 32 phase states remains < ±0.4 dB, which eases the calibration of the phased-array system.

articleTitle: A 4×25-Gb/s Serializer with Integrated CDR and 3-Tap FFE Driver for NIC Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a four-channel voltage-mode serializer in 40-nm CMOS for network interface card (NIC) optical interconnects. Each channel is designed by a quarter-rate clock and data recovery (CDR) with digital loop filter, which recovers the data received by analog front-end circuits. A source-series-terminated (SST) driver employs three groups of slices in parallel to achieve multi-tap configurable equalization. A shared phase-locked loop is integrated to provide a 25-GHz global clock for all the channels. The serializer works from 1-V supply with 163 mW power when the CDR is enabled, and consumes 36.2 mW in the pseudo-random bit sequence (PRBS) testing mode. The post-layout simulation results show clean output eye diagrams at 25-Gb/s datarate. The differential output swing reaches 1.07 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ppd</inf> and the jitter is less than 2.5 ps.

articleTitle: A Portable Accelerator of Proximal Policy Optimization for Robots
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Reinforcement learning has great potential to solve robotic controlling tasks for different environments. Proximal policy optimization (PPO) is one of the most efficient algorithms of reinforcement learning, which implements three neural net-works during the training and inference. However, the practical applications of reinforcement learning algorithms in robots are limited by the computational complexity of the neural networks. An accelerator for PPO is proposed based on high level synthesis (HLS) in this work, which accelerates both training and inference. The proposed accelerator design is implemented on Ultra96-v2 FPGA board with Pynq system and is suitable for different robotic applications. The proposed accelerator design on programmable logic (PL) achieves 16.8x improvement in the training process and 12.4x in the inference compared to processing system (PS). Meanwhile, the proposed accelerator runs at a similar speed with PC while achieving a 93.3% power reduction.

articleTitle: A 5.72-μW, 1.02-MHz, -40~125°C, 1μs-Startup Time Relaxation Oscillation with Fully-on-Chip Voltage Reference and LDO Regulator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 1.02 MHz 5.72-μW 60-ppm/°C relaxation oscillator is demonstrated in a 180-nm CMOS process. The proposed oscillator simplifies the logic control circuits to save power consumption and chip area. By employing an improved delay compensation technique, the proposed oscillator has minimized sensitivity to temperature variations. The measured results show an average frequency drift of about 60 ppm/°C and a power consumption of below 6 μW. For a supply voltage change of from 1.1V to 2 V, the frequency changes within only ± 1.6%.

articleTitle: Design of an Exponential Current Generator for Neural Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new exponential current generation circuit design for neural stimulation. The use of exponential output current can improve the power efficiency. The proposed exponential current generator is designed based on the Taylor series approximation, which can produce the continuous-time exponential decaying current with improved dynamic range and accuracy. The circuit is designed based on 180 nm CMOS process in Cadence. Simulation results show the relative error is smaller than 1% when the pulse width is 700 μs. The maximum current decaying dynamic ratio of the stimulator is 11.96 dB, which is improved by 2.3 times compared with similar neural stimulators.

articleTitle: HARNS: High-level Architectural Model of RRAM based Computing-in-memory NPU
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As the research on deep neural networks booms, there is broad interest in the accelerator with RRAM-based computing-in-memory architecture to tackle the problem of "memory wall". However, the simulator for large-scale RRAM-based SoC, expected to provide detailed performance analysis, remains unexplored. In this paper, we develop HARNS in C++ and SystemC, an architectural model of RRAM-based neural-processing-unit. HARNS proposes a flexible structure for users to customize the architecture, and provides cycle-accurate performance simulation for design space exploration. A 7-layer convolution network is demonstrated on HARNS, followed by some optimization schemes of architecture and mapping.

articleTitle: Development of an Inkjet-Printed Interdigitated Device: CAD, Fabrication, and Testing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This work is aimed at the analysis of an inkjet-printed one-port interdigitated device. After using computer-aided design (CAD) simulation tools for an effective design optimization, the proposed interdigitated device has been fabricated by using the inkjet-printing technology. The performance of the device under test (DUT) has been verified through an experimental characterization carried out with a vector network analyzer (VNA). Experiments have bee made in the frequency range from 100 MHz to 6 GHz.

articleTitle: A Data Non-destructive IMPLY-based Memristive Semi-parallel Full-Adder for Computing-in-memory Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a data non-destructive IMPLY-based memristive semi-parallel full-adder (FA) for Computing-in-memory system, which solves the issue that the conventional semi-parallel FA cannot protect the input operands. The proposed full adder not only reduce the operating time by executing more steps in parallel, and also prevent the input operands from being destructed by adding an extra memristor with only one additional step. Simulation results show that the proposed full adder can realize 18% reduction on operation time against the conventional design, while protect the input operand from destruction, which is an efficient design for data reuse in neural network acceleration.

articleTitle: A High Power Supply Rejection and Low Noise Low-Dropout Regulator for Voltage Controlled Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Low-dropout regulator (LDO) is normally used to provide good supply quality for voltage controlled oscillator (VCO). In this work, the requirements of PSR and output noise of LDO are analyzed and obtained by restricting the deterioration of VCO’s phase noise. Then the PSR of the LDO is modeled and a method to get high PSR and low output noise LDO is proposed. Finally, a capacitor-less LDO is designed by using the proposed method with a standard 28 nm CMOS process. The PSRs of designed LDO are - 81 dB at 10 kHz and - 41 dB at 1 MHz, respectively. The integrated noise is 3.9 µVrms among the frequency range of 10 Hz ~ 100 kHz. The LDO has a small output capacitor of 15 pF, and the quiescent current is only 100 μA.

articleTitle: An energy-efficient and high-PSNR image denoising pre-processor based on optimized non-local means algorithm for real-time FHD video applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Image is widely used in many fields as an important information carrier. In embedded devices, denoise as an important part of image processing will obviously affect the result. The progress of sensor resolution and light-sensitive capability has higher requirements for denoise speed and quality. Most of the embedded cameras can only perform noise reduction based on simple local denoising with unsatisfactory results due to resource constraints, while the non-local denoising with better results has high computational complexity and is difficult to achieve real-time processing in embedded applications. In this paper, an energy-efficient and high-PSNR image denoising pre-processor based on optimized NLM algorithm is proposed with following features: i) optimized parameters in the weight function and the utilized method noise to improve the denoising performance; ii) a customized systolic array with full pipelining to achieve high processing throughput; iii) a data reuse strategy to reduce the frequent data movement for high energy-efficiency. The achieved results of 22.8 mJ/frame and 765μJ/frame in 110-nm ASIC and Xillinx Zynq FPGA shows that the proposed design is a competitive energy-efficient solution for many mobile FHD video applications.

articleTitle: Resonant Gate Driver for High Speed GaN HMET with dV/dt Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the increase of switching frequency, high power density converters require extremely urgent requirements for low power loss, high ring suppression and EMI optimization for the drivers. This work proposes a novel resonant gate driver designed for high frequency E-mode GaN HEMT power devices that can flexibly online configure the power device's turn-on and turn-off dV/dt. DV/dt can change by more than 6 times with the help of bias of auxiliary transistors, respectively. The calculated data is provided to optimize the efficiency and EMI noise. Meanwhile the topology can reduce the sensitivity of gate parasitic inductance to avoid incorrect operation. These operations of the proposed resonant gate driver are verified by utilizing 100V GaN HEMT.

articleTitle: A Low-Power RC Oscillator with Offset and Path Delay Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 128-kHz RC time-constant-based relaxation oscillator is designed in 180-nm CMOS for ultra-low-power applications. The chopping structure and replica path delay loop are employed in this work to eliminate the effect of comparator offset and path delay respectively, leading to a frequency accuracy of ±0.21% over the temperature range from -20°C to 100 °C. The power consumption is 344 nW with 0.8-V supply, resulting in an energy of 1.55 nW/kHz.

articleTitle: A 25nA IQ, 20mA ILOAD OCL-LDO for Battery-Powered IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An output-capacitorless low-dropout regulator using adaptive biasing and two cross-summed transconductance cells has been presented in this paper. The proposed LDO has been designed in 65nm CMOS technology. The simulated quiescent current is 25 nA under zero loading condition, and the maximum loading capability is 20 mA. Good stability is achieved under full load range and 0~100pF output capacitance. Moreover, it can work under 1.4~4.2V supply voltage range, making it suitable for battery-powered IoT devices. The simulated voltage spike is less than 275 mV when loading current changing between 200 μA and 20 mA with 10ns edge time, which corresponds to a FOM of 0.00035 ps.

articleTitle: A 1.2 ppm/°C TC, 0.094% Inaccuracy 3-18 V Supply-Range Bandgap Reference with Self-Compensation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a low temperature coefficient (TC) bandgap reference (BGR) with self-compensation through curvature function. The offset and noise suppression technique are employed to achieve high accuracy. In order to have a wide supply voltage ranging from 3 to 18 V and a load current range from -5 to 10 mA, a pre-regulator and class-AB output stage are introduced. The proposed BGR is implemented in a 0.18 µm BCD CMOS process and the active area is 345 × 420 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulation results show that the TC is 1.2 ppm/°C. The variation coefficient σ/µ of the output voltage is 0.094%.

articleTitle: A 12bit 100fs Resolution Multi-Stage Digital-to-Time Converter with Dynamic Element Matching
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 12bit 100fs resolution Digital-to-Time Converter (DTC) for frac-N PLL is proposed. To avoid the linearity degradation of a single stage DTC covering a large delay range, the DTC is implemented in a multistage topology, with multiple DTC stages cascaded in series. Global Dynamic Element Matching (DEM) and data segmentation are adopted to suppress the impact of mismatch. The proposed DTC is designed and simulated in a 28nm CMOS process. It achieves 12bit accuracy with 100fs resolution and 400ps range while running at 100 MHz. INL and DNL are below 0.3 LSB and 0.1 LSB respectively. Simulated phase noise is below -160 dBc/Hz at 100kHz offset. The total power consumption is 3.3mW under 1V supply. And the occupied area is 0.067mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 2GS/s 12bit Time-Interleaved Pipelined ADC in 40nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes design of a 2GS/s 12bit 4-channel time-interleaved (TI) pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC) in 40nm CMOS. To decrease ADC power, both amplifier and reference circuits are shared by each two channels. A 1.5bit-per-stage architecture and SHA-less stages are adopted to optimize channel sampling rate and power consumption. The TI ADC inter-stage-gain and inter-channel errors are eliminated by Least Mean Square (LMS)-based and correlation-based digital calibrations respectively. Simulation results show that the calibrated pipelined ADC reaches 10.2bit ENOB and 74.5dB SFDR, with a 2GS/s sample rate and a Nyquist input. The ADC power dissipation is 624mW, corresponding to an excellent FoM of 261.6fJ/con.

articleTitle: A 25-to-40 GHz Asymmetric Single-Pole Double-Throw Switch Using Triple-Well CMOS Device
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 25-40 GHz wideband single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch for 5G applications. It is based on an asymmetrical structure in which two stacked transistors are used in transmitter side to maintain low insertion loss and high linearity in Tx mode. Inductors are used to resonate with capacitors to realize a wideband impedance matching. The measurement results of the proposed SPDT switch achieves an insertion loss (IL) of 2.0/2.5 dB and an isolation (ISO) of 20/16 dB across 25-40 GHz in Tx/Rx mode respectively. When operating in transmit mode, the simulated input 1dB compression point (IP1dB) of the switch is 19.8 dBm. The chip core area occupies 0.18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Mismatch of nonlinear stiffness in differential MEMS resonating sensors and its self-test and calibration technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a self-test and calibration technique for differential MEMS resonating sensors to reduce the flicker noise due to nonlinear stiffness mismatch. By properly adjusting reference voltages on two channels respectively, the amplitude-frequency gain of two oscillators become the same and the flicker noise can be cancelled out. A simulation model is established based on mechanical parameters obtained from experiment results, which reveals that the long term bias-instability of MEMS sensor is reduced by 60.3%.

articleTitle: Towards Intelligent-Edge Computing: Application, Architecture, Circuit, and Device Perspective
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the development of algorithm and hardware, the new computing paradigm changes from the centralized intelligence on cloud computing to the distributed intelligence on edge computing. On the algorithm hand, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been applied to a variety of disciplines and proved highly successful in a vast class of intelligent-edge applications cross many domains, such as wearable devices, biomedical monitoring systems, and internet-of-things. On the hardware hand, edge computing has been widely recognized as a promising solution to meet the requirements of low latency, high scalability and energy efficiency. For AI with edge computing, an issue is limited resources for computations and communications. In this paper, we investigate effective solutions for intelligent-edge computing algorithms, hardware architecture, circuit design and emerging technology.

articleTitle: Randomly-Accessible Active Pixel Sensor with Wide Dynamic Range and Reduced Fixed Pattern Noise
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The classical logarithmic active pixel sensor is susceptible to fixed pattern noise, giving rise to dark signal non-uniformity. In this work, this long-standing issue is resolved by introducing a reference pixel sub-sensor adjacent to an active working sub-sensor with the same design. The differential signal of these two sub-sensors will be used as output signal and thus fixed pattern noise is reduced. Such a randomly-accessible active pixel sensor also exhibits an adjustable sensitivity from 0.3 A/W to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> A/W in the visible light spectrum and a wide dynamic range of over 120 dB, making it functionally similar to the photoreceptor of the human retina.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time MASH Delta-Sigma Modulator with an IIR-based Self-Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a self-coupled discrete-time multistage noise-shaping (MASH) delta-sigma modulator (DSM) with using an infinite impulse-response (IIR) filter between two stages. By introducing an IIR filter into the self-coupled path, the proposed MASH DSM could compensate the loss of maximum stable amplitude (MSA) owing to the injected self-coupled path. A larger MSA results in a higher power efficiency. Moreover, the IIR filter is implemented as first-order without imposing explicit hardware complexity. The behavioral-level simulations confirm the concept of the proposed MASH DSM.

articleTitle: A Pixel-Parallel Array Processor without Computational Logic for Computational Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A pixel-parallel array processor without computational logic is proposed towards compact computational image sensors. By utilizing a multiplexer-based functionality paradigm, this processor saves a considerable amount of chip resources. It was prototyped on an FPGA with typical algorithm demonstrations. The experimental results show that our processor consumes much less logic resources than prior works while keeping comparable processing performance.

articleTitle: A 40nm 33.6Tops/W 8T-SRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro with DAC-less Spike-Pulse-Truncation Input and ADC-less Charge-Reservoir-Integrate-Counter Output
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a DAC-less and ADC-less 8T-SRAM CIM macro, which converts digital input-activation into spike pulse sequence based on a novel DAC-less pulse truncation unit and employs an ADC-less charge-reservoir-integrate counter for result output. Our design can significantly reduce area and energy overhead of the DAC and ADC circuits. Further, a system-level variation-tolerant quantization/training method by exploiting the hardware features was proposed to guarantee computing accuracy. A 4-Kb 8T-SRAM CIM macro with 4-bit input, 4-bit weight and 4-bit output was fabricated using a foundry’s 40-nm CMOS process. Our test results show that the chip achieves energy efficiency of 33.6 Tops/W under 4-bit input and 4-bit weight precision, supporting the connection of intelligent things with high computing efficiency and low energy.

articleTitle: FWUA : A Flexible Winograd-Based Uniform Accelerator for 1D/2D/3D CNNs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven to be promising in various applications such as audio recognition, image classification, and video understanding. Different dimensions of CNNs (e.g., 1D, 2D, and 3D CNNs) are proposed to adapt to these applications. To accelerate different dimensional convolution, a uniform accelerator is necessary. Nevertheless, the implementation poses a significant challenge due to several observations. Firstly, computational complexity, network mapping methods, and data reuse strategies vary greatly among different dimensional convolutional neural networks. Secondly, various efficient algorithms such as Winograd have been proposed to accelerate CNNs, but their implementations lack flexible support for different network types. Typically, the Winograd-base accelerator is designed for 1-stride and the non-1-stride methods haven’t been implemented on 3D CNNs. To address these challenges, we propose a flexible Winograd-based uniform accelerator (FWUA) for 1D/2D/3D CNNs. With adaptive support for different dimensions, strides, and filter sizes, FWUA is runtime-reconfigurable for different dimensions of CNNs applications, i.e., audio, image, and video. The FWUA is verified on the Xilinx ZCU102 evaluation board FPGA. Our design achieves 1.51/1.13/0.66 (GOPS/DSP) DSP-efficiency and 242/181/105 (GOPS/W) energy-efficiency in C3D, VGG-16, and HAR-CNNs, which are up to 2x comparing to state-of-the-art FPGA works.

articleTitle: SiC Trench MOSFET with N-base Super Barrier Rectifier Embedded for Optimizing Reverse Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel double trench SiC MOSFET embedded with N-base super barrier rectifier (NSBR-DTMOS) is proposed in this paper. The NSBR-DTMOS exhibits its diode turn on voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>) half lower than that of body diode. With the super barrier rectifier (SBR) embedded as the freewheeling diode, the bipolar degradation phenomena caused by the body diode is eliminated successfully. Compared with the conventional DTMOS, the gate-to-drain capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>) and gate-drain charge (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>) are reduced by half, at the cost of the specific ON-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>) increases by 9% only. As a result, the figures of merit R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>×Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>×Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf> are improved by 45% and 54% respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Area-Efficient Fast CORDIC for Energy-efficient Adaptive Exponential Integrate and Fire Neuron Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The realization of bionic neural models has great challenges on the biological characteristics and hardware efficiency of neurons. This paper proposes an energy efficient Adaptive Exponential Integrate and Fire (AdEx) neuron based on a novel Area-Efficient Fast COordinate Rotation Digital Computer (AEF-CORDIC). The novel AEF-CORDIC has a higher energy efficiency and shorter latency by reducing the iteration times with negligible hardware overhead. FPGA implementation results show that the proposed AEF-CORDIC based AdEx Neuron has good biological characteristics. Compared with conventional CORDIC based design, our design has 48.4% and 52.5% improvement on energy efficiency and processing speed, respectively.

articleTitle: A 96% Peak Efficiency Off-chip Capacitor Free Dimmable Hysteresis Current Control LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated buck-type dimmable synchronous LED driver for high-brightness solid-state lighting applications. A high-side gate driver based on linear regulator is proposed to drive power pMOS without any external off-chip components. Implemented in a 0.18 μm 30V BCD process, the proposed LED driver supports a wide input range from 6V to 30V,operates up to 1MHz and delivers an average LED current of 700 mA for driving up to 9 series-connected HB-LEDs. The proposed LED driver achieves a peak power efficiency of 96% and the current deviation ＜3.1% of the average LED current under different conditions.

articleTitle: An E-Band CMOS Frequency Quadrupler with 1.7-dBm Output Power and 45-dB Fundamental Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an E-band frequency quadrupler, utilizing two push-push frequency doublers and two single-stage neutralized amplifiers. The pseudo-differential class-B biased cascode topology is adopted for frequency doubler, which improves the reverse isolation and conversion gain. Two amplifiers are designed based on neutralization technique, which increases the stability and power gain simultaneously. The stacked transformers are used for power matching and single-ended-to-differential transformation. Fabricated in 40-nm CMOS, the measurement results show a maximum output power and conversion gain of 1.7 dBm and 3.4 dB, respectively at 76 GHz. Fundamental and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-harmonic suppressions of better than 45 dB and 20 dB are achieved over the desired bandwidth.

articleTitle: Modeling of Hot Carrier Injection on Gate-Induced Drain Leakage in PDSOI nMOSFET
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL) current in partial depleted silicon on insulator nMOSFET was measured under different hot carrier injection conditions. With the increase of stress time, the GIDL current increases steeply under channel hot carrier condition due to the dominant electron injection into oxide and the consequent generation of interface traps. On the other hand, under the drain avalanche hot carrier condition, the additional hole injection partially cancels with the electrons, leading to a mild increase of GIDL current. By taking into account the interface traps induced threshold voltage shift, we further proposed a modified model to fit the experimental data.

articleTitle: An Area-Saving Balun for Multiband IoT Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Herein an on-chip area-saving balun is presented for a multiband transmitter that supports all the commonly used standards (NB-IoT, BLE and ZigBee) in low-rate IoT. By switching the effective number of coil turns in this balun, it can guarantee a Q value higher than 10 and provide the required inductance to supporting three-bands (LB: 824-915 MHz, MB: 1695-1710 MHz, HB: 2400-2483 MHz). Compared with the traditional multi-transformer design method in multiband transmitter, the tunable balun can effectively save the chip area. The proposed balun was designed in a 65-nm RF CMOS process, its total area is only 0.14 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Simulation results show that its insertion loss is less than -3.1dB, the amplitude and phase balance are both with in 1.2dB and 1°.

articleTitle: Anomalous NMOSFET hot carrier degradation on DRAM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Anomalous NMOS HCI degradation has been reported on logic IC and NAND. This paper presents for the first time its occurrence on DRAM. It also shows the trade-off between DRAM retention and peripheral circuit HCI related reliability. The underlying mechanism is fully verified through systemic investigation on electrical characteristics including the subthreshold leakage increasing and recovery, DIBL worsening, and different IDS degradation behavior in linear and saturation regions. These interesting behaviors are strongly process dependent and associated with interface state generation. This work provides some ideas to minimize the anomalous degradation risk.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Analog Frontend with Large PD Capacitance Tolerance in 65-nm CMOS for Optical Receivers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-noise analog frontend circuit for optical receivers, which can tolerate relatively large photodiode (PD) parasitic capacitance while ensuring the required bandwidth and sensitivity for a given data rate. The proposed circuit includes a high-gm transimpedance amplifier (TIA) with a three-stage class-AB topology and large feedback resistance to suppress the input-referred noise so as to improve the sensitivity of the receiver, while employs bandwidth extension structures in the cascaded limiting amplifier and output driver to overcome the noise–bandwidth tradeoff. Designed in 65-nm CMOS, post-layout simulation shows that the circuit achieves an optical modulation amplitude (OMA) sensitivity of -17.98 dBm at 10 Gb/s for BER=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup>, and a bandwidth of 7.98 GHz, under an overall parasitic input parasitic capacitance of 467 fF.

articleTitle: A 0.45-V 3.3-µW Resistor-Based Temperature Sensor Achieving 10mK Resolution in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 0.45-V resistor-based temperature sensor for energy-harvested Internet-of-Things device is presented. The sub-0.5-V operation is achieved by introducing a digital-intensive frequency-locked loop to convert the temperature-sensitive resistance to timing information. To overcome the high on-resistance of the transistors at sub-0.5 V, we apply gate-bulk-connected transistors to improve the on-resistance while safeguarding their leakages in the off-state. Simulated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the temperature sensor consumes 3.3 µW at room temperature. With a 10-ms conversion time, the temperature sensor can achieve a resolution of 10 mK, resulting in a resolution FoM of 3.3 pJ•K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of a X-Band 2×2 Phased-Array Transceiver Module Using Chiplet Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: radio frequency (RF) microsystem, which uses advanced heterogeneous integration (hetero-structure and hetero-material integration) package, has been widely attracted. In order to acquire more efficient design of complex RF microsystem, the method of chiplet based on accurate chip model (Intellectual Property, IP) is studied in this paper. Four RF chips are modeled and applied to design a X-band phased array T/R module. Compared with traditional design, the modified method can improve simulation accuracy of module.

articleTitle: A 32×32 Array Terahertz Sensor in 65-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 32×32 array CMOS terahertz sensor. It is implemented using a 65-nm standard CMOS process, integrates a 32×32 pixel array and parallelized readout circuits (ROICs) into a single silicon chip. The pixel detector is proposed strictly compatible with process design rules. The full chip occupies a 2.81×5.39 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area. Voltage responsivity(Rv) of 701 V/W and readout speed of 319 fps are reported.

articleTitle: Characteristics of A Novel Quaternary Tunneling Field-Effect Transistor for Low Power Applicaitons
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The application of multivalued devices in the logic circuits is considered as one of the most promising approaches to simultaneously overcome the power scaling challenges and increase the information density. The negative differential resistance devices and quantum dot gate FETs are mainly introduced to realize the multiple states. However, both of the aforementioned devices are currently limited to ternary device demonstrations owning to the formation mechanism of the intermediate state. In the article, a novel quarternary device based on the band-to-band tunneling is proposed. By the adoption of large gate-to-source overlap and the modulation of the doping concentration in the source, four stable and distinctive states can be achieved, which means that area efficiency and energy efficiency is improved significantly compared with the conventional binary logic systems. Besides, small supply voltage and low OFF-state current can be obtained at the same time, which would promote the introduction of the multistate devices in ultralow-power logic circuits.

articleTitle: Optimization methods for high inductance-density inductors for high speed integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As the high speed integrated circuit developing, the number of on-chip inductors in single chip becomes larger. To overcome annoying electromagnetic crosstalk between metal coils, the 8-shaped inductors are promoted. However, the 8-shaped inductors suffer from poor expansion for multiple turns and thus can only achieve relatively low inductance. This work propose structures aimed at enhancing 8-shaped inductor’s inductance-density, improving chip integration under the premise of small electromagnetic crosstalk, and providing differentiable topology.

articleTitle: High-Throughput Zipper Encoder for 800G Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: After 400G fiber-optical communication standard is proposed, considerable attention has been paid to the next-generation optical network. In this paper, we propose a zipper encoder architecture with low-overhead memory and optimized BCH encoder. Working at 500MHz, the zipper encoder can achieve throughput of 962Gbps, which meets the requirement of 800G optical communication system. The whole design was implemented with Design Compiler in the TSMC 65nm. Result shows that our design achieves 1.8x/1.7x energy-efficiency and 2.2x/1.2x area-efficiency higher than prior 200G/400G staircase encoders.

articleTitle: Design of an ultra-low Power MFCC Feature Extraction Circuit with Embedded Speech Activity Detector
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Mel frequency cepstrum coefficient (MFCC) is widely used in the feature extraction of speech signals. In practical applications, the feature extraction circuit does not need to work at non-speech conditions. By extracting and reusing the data of framing operation in MFCC, we propose a speech activity detector (SAD) based on the amplitude and zero-crossing rate of the speech to distinguish different states of it. This SAD uses time-domain characteristics of the signal to achieve low power design, its recognition rate is 95.1% at the noiseless environment and 94.6% with a signal-to-noise rate of 20dB. Designed in TSMC 28nm CMOS process, 40kHz and 0.41V supply, the simulation results show that the power is 0.007/0.34 respectively at non-speech and full-speech segments. The long-term average power is only 24 at the typical application with an event rate of 720/h.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Low Noise Amplifier Design in 0.13-um CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband low noise amplifier (LNA) fabricated in 130-nm CMOS technology. A shunt resistor feedback topology combined with transformer matching is proposed and used to broaden the bandwidth. The measured results show that this single-stage LNA has an operation band ranging from 6.5 GHz to 13.5 GHz in terms of the 3-dB drop in gain, which defines a relative bandwidth of 70%. In addition, the LNA may achieve the minimum noise figure (NF) of 3.9 dB at 9 GHz and the maximum gain of 8.7 dB at 8 GHz. The 1-dB compression point of input power is -4 dBm at 8 GHz. The area of the LNA is 0.36 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including the RF and DC pads.

articleTitle: A New Method to Extract Mobility Degradation and Parasitic Series Resistance of Nano-scaled MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A new method is proposed to extract the parasitic series resistance and mobility degradation for nano-scaled MOSFET, which requires only simple dc measurements. The proposed method is based on the shift-and-ratio method and takes into account the degradation of effective mobility with gate length. Compared with the traditional method, it does not require to know the threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) and effective channel length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>), which avoids the error caused by inaccurate extraction of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>. The proposed method was carefully examined using TCAD simulation data of 90 nm MOSFET.

articleTitle: Large On/Off and Rectification Ratios, Self-Compliance, High-Uniformity in Pt/Al2O3/TaOx/Ta Self-Rectifying Memristors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Since the self-rectifying memristor (SRM) can effectively mitigate the sneak path problem, it is favored by researchers for large-scale passive crossbar arrays. We successfully fabricated a prominent Pt/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/TaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/Ta bilayer SRM device (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> on/off ratio, ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> rectification ratio, and high-uniformity) with a 100-μm feature size. A ~1 μA self-compliance current and <10 nA operation current are also achieved in this device. Moreover, on the premise of 10% read margin (RM), the maximum crossbar array scale can reach 133 kb. Finally, the switching and rectifying mechanisms of the Pt/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/TaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/Ta SRM device are analyzed by band diagram. This bilayer structure SRM may provide a promising candidate for 3D integration.

articleTitle: A 10-Mbps 119.2-pJ/bit Software Defined Body Channel Transceiver Employing a CCII-based PGA and a 2.5-bit/cycle ADC in 180-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a BCC transceiver designed for softeware-defined applications. In the RX side, a novel 2.5 bit/cycle structure is adopt in 5-bit SAR ADC for fast-converging sampling. Before the ADC, a PGA based on CCII amplifies the signal with improved energy efficiency. In the TX side, a DAC-like body driver is utilized to transmits PAM4 signal into human body with boosted bandwidth utilization. Fabricated in 180 nm CMOS process and under 1.5 V supply, it achieves 10 Mbps with 119.2 pJ/bit efficiency.

articleTitle: A Symmetric Multilayer GeSe/GeSeSbTe Ovonic Threshold Switching Selector with Improved Endurance and Stability
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) selector is becoming the most suitable candidate for selector devices in memristor crossbar array, owing to its high selectivity and fast response time. However, device endurance and variance are persistent tricky problems for application. In this article, a novel symmetric multilayer OTS selector based on simple GeSe and SbTe-doped GeSe was investigated. The results showed improving selector performed extraordinary endurance up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> and the fluctuation of threshold voltage is 1.5 %. These developments pave the way towards tuning a new class of OTS materials engineering, ensuring improvement of electrical performances.

articleTitle: TripleBrain: An Edge Neuromorphic Architecture for High-accuracy Single-layer Spiking Neural Network with On-chip Self-organizing and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a scalable, high-performance and cost-effective digital neuromorphic hardware architecture for a single-layer SNN model, with fast and accurate on-chip learning capability. To obtain high recognition accuracies while reducing resource cost and processing latency, our neuromorphic architecture combines three brain-inspired factors: the SNN framework, the neuromorphic self-organizing map (SOM) learning (i.e., the unsupervised SOM-STDP learning rule), and the biological reinforcement learning (i.e., the reward-modulated STDP or R-STDP learning rule). Our hardware architecture mainly consists of a parallel and scalable 2D array of sub-network tiles, each computing 8×8 spiking neurons. On the hardware, a single-layer SNN is first trained by the SOM-STDP rule, and then fine-tuned by the R-STDP rule to improve the recognition accuracy. It realized a high performance of 448 frames/s during learning and 1818 fps during inference on the MNIST image dataset, at a 200 MHz clock frequency and 0.95 W power consumption. It attained high accuracies of 95.24% and 81.4% on the MNIST and ETH-80 datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Power Fully Differential Voltage-to-Time Converter with DC Offset Calibration for RF Wake-Up Receivers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An ultra-low power fully differential voltage-to-time converter (VTC) with DC offset calibration is proposed, which is applied to the differential baseband receiving path of the wake-up receiver (WuRx). The combination of the loop technology that can effectively calibrate the offset and the differential structure that can suppress noise and common-mode interference reduces the false alarm rate of the WuRx, improving the sensitivity and robustness. In addition, the VTC has the characteristic of low-pass filtering, which can omit the low-pass filter (LPF) module and greatly reduce the area. The proposed VTC is designed in TSMC 65nm LP CMOS process with a core size of 0.0552 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The supply voltage is 0.4 V, facing the DC offset voltage is 2mV and the sampling period is 2ms, the offset voltage tends to be stable within 12ms. After calibration, the equivalent input offset is reduced from 2mV to 22 μV. The VTC is highly stable during the whole process, and the power consumption is as low as 5nW.

articleTitle: In-MRAM Computing Elements with Single-Step Convolution and Fully Connected for BNN/TNN
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In-memory computing shows great energy-efficient attraction in non-von Neumann architecture. Computing in spin-transfer-torque magnetic RAM (STT-MRAM) is expected to achieve both ultra-low-power and interconnection delay reduction. In this work, a 4T2M MRAM bit-cell and associated peripheral circuits are proposed, which can perform XNOR operation and ternary operation extension in-memory. At the same time, a one-step 3×3 binary convolution method and a ternary fully connected operation are proposed. MNIST data sets are used to verify the designed neural network, the accuracy is over 95%, and the one-step convolution can save more than 50% of energy consumption compared to the traditional row-by-row calculation.

articleTitle: A 39GHz Divide-by-8 LC-Ring ILFD Designed for 5G New Radio n260 Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a 39GHz divide-by-8 LC-Ring ILFD designed for 5G new radio n260 band. The proposed LCRing ILFD is composed of a divide-by-2 LC ILFD and divide-by-4 Ring ILFD for wide locking range with small area and low power consumption. By impedance matching using transmission lines between the two ILFDs, the injection power into divide-by-4 Ring ILFD is increased. The core area of this circuit is 0.38mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in 65nm CMOS process. The total locking range of this LC-Ring ILFD is 35.4-43.7GHz (21.0%) with a power consumption of 6.5mW.

articleTitle: A Fast-Transient Capacitor-Less Low-Dropout Regulator for Wideband Optical Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A capacitor-less fast-transient-response low-dropout regulator (FTR-LDO) is presented for wideband optical links. A transient-enhanced loop (TEL) is proposed to form a local high-speed path at output, which detects and responses to the output. A transient-transferring capacitor (TTC) is employed to reduce the response time of total FTR-LDO. A power supply rejection (PSR) capacitor is added at the gate of the power transistor (PT) to suppress common-mode noise. The FTR-LDO could be more suitable for system-on-chip (SoC) applications, wideband optical transceivers included. Implemented in 180 nm SiGe BiCMOS, the FTR-LDO is simulated with 0.9 V dropout voltage, -15 dB PSR over DC-100-GHz bandwidth, and up to 38 mV transient fluctuations when loaded with a 56 Gb/s trans-impedance amplifier (TIA).

articleTitle: Efficient VLSI Architecture for Edge Sensing Anti-Aliasing Demosaicing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The majority of digital cameras reconstruct full-color images from raw data captured by image sensors through a process called demosaicing. In this paper, we propose an edge sensing anti-aliasing demosaicing (ESAAD) algorithm for the Bayer pattern, which is the most widely used color filter array (CFA) layout, and an efficient very-large-scale integration (VLSI) architecture for hardware implementation of the ESAAD. Traditional demosaicing methods recover the RGB channels of pixels on and not on edges in the same way while ESAAD detects edges from the RAW images and recovers pixels on and not on edges by different strategies. In this way, we can improve the visuality of recovered edges greatly compared with previous demosaicing methods. In addition, the simplicity of the ESAAD enables a hardware-friendly VLSI architecture which only requires 2 lines of line buffers. Under the same conditions of the process technology with 180nm CMOS, the image resolution with 1280×720 (HD), and the working frequency with 200MHz, the performance of this work significantly outperforms all the other methods on resources usage including both gate counts and core area, and power consumption.

articleTitle: A protection chip for three lithium cells
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper designs a 3-cell lithium battery charge and discharge protection chip based on the 0.18 µm Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process. The measurements indicate that the chip can reliably transfer the voltage of each cell and take protective measures against abnormal circumstances, such as overvoltage, undervoltage and overcurrent. Besides, the voltage detection circuit reduces the leakage current, which is beneficial to extend the service time of the battery pack.

articleTitle: A Dual-Channel Switching-Linear Series-Connected Hybrid Dynamic Power Supply with Dual-Supply LDOs for Thermo-Optical Tuning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel switching-linear series-connected hybrid dynamic power supply with dual-supply LDOs for thermo-optical tuning is proposed in this paper. The proposed design leverages the intrinsic dual supplies to extend the operating range of the LDOs. It can simultaneously regulate two output channels, and track 100 kHz 0.4 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PP</inf> sinusoidal waveforms. Significant efficiency improvement of the proposed design is achieved for envelope signals with a small difference, which is common in thermo-optical tuning. The proposed design is implemented in 130nm CMOS process, and achieves a peak efficiency of 87.9% at 1.2 V driving a 60 Ω load. Its dynamic efficiency is about 85%.

articleTitle: Design of 77GHz Automotive Radar Antenna Based on FOWLP
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents the integration of 77-GHz antennas with a 77-GHz transceiver chip on fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) with a compact size of 13 × 13 × 0.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for automotive radar systems. The antenna consists of two transmitting antennas and two receiving antennas. H-shape slot coupled patch arrays are chosen as the antenna radiators.The system covers the 77-GHz band and achieves the maximal peak realized gains of 7.11 dB and 12.11 dB for transmitting and receiving antennas, respectively. The isolation between transmitting and receiving ports is lower than -25dB in 77-GHz band.

articleTitle: A Power-Efficient Specific Emitter Identification Hardware Accelerator With SNR-Aware Adaptive Precision Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Specific emitter identification (SEI) plays a crucial role in spectrum management applications. Recently many SEI algorithms based on deep convolution neural network (DCNN) have been proposed. However, the high computational complexity of DCNN leads to large power consumption. Also, there is a lack of dedicated SEI hardware design. In this work, we proposed a SNR-aware adaptive scalable SEI algorithm based on DCNN, and implemented a power-efficient SEI hardware accelerator based on it. The SEI hardware accelerator can adaptively reconfigures itself between 16-bit weight computing mode and binary weight computing mode by sensing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) condition to improve power efficiency while maintaining high accuracy. The experiment results show that our accelerator can achieve a high power efficiency of 6.51Gops/W for the high SNR condition and a high accuracy of 80% in the low SNR condition, compared with conventional non-adaptive designs with 16-bit or binary computing mode.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Design of Large Fan-in Dynamic One-hot Multiplexer in 28nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: We propose an energy-efficient large fan-in one-hot dynamic logic multiplexer (OHDL-MUX) for the design of low-power large-scale digital integrated circuits. It is composed of a specific pulse generator, dynamic AND-OR cells and a dynamic OR cell. Conventionally, a large fan-in CMOS MUX is composed of large number of standard cells with a large delay, power and area overhead. For significantly improving the circuits’ energy efficiency, three techniques are used to achieve ultra low-power consumption: 1) dynamic logic is adopted to reduce internal nodal parasitic capacitance. 2) A dynamic AND-OR cell and a dynamic OR cell with very few transistors are designed. 3) A specific pulse generator is designed to reduce the flip of clock signal and signal dispersion. Implemented in TSMC 28-nm technology, this MUX consumes 17.14μw at 0.9V and 1.0 GHz, with an area of 246.63 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Compared to the conventional CMOS MUX, 21.3%, 33.4% and 80.9% reduction in delay, power consumption and layout area is achieved, respectively.

articleTitle: Pulsed Operation on HfO2/Al2O3 RRAM Device as Electronic Dendrite
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based resistive random-access memory (RRAM) devices were fabricated to research the device characteristics for electronic dendrite application. We used different forms of pulses to control the states of RRAM to realize the dendritic function. The noise signal filtering and nonlinear integration function had been realized in the RRAM devices. The influence of pulse width on threshold voltage had also been researched, and the continuous pulse was used to research the stability of on/off state. Besides, we researched the energy consumption of noise signal filtering and nonlinear integration function. These research shows that the independent device of the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based RRAM structure can simulate the function of dendrites and has lower energy consumption.

articleTitle: A 1st-order noise shaping SAR ADC with dual-capacitor merge-and-split switching scheme for sensor chip
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>-order noise shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is presented with the dual-capacitor merge-and-split (DCMS) switching scheme for low-power sensing applications. The proposed switching scheme features the constant common-mode voltage, so the dynamic offset can be relaxed obviously. Meanwhile, compared to the conventional switching scheme, the proposed switching scheme achieves 99.22% reduction in average switching energy and 50% capacitor area saving due to only using the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cm</inf> reference level. Simulation results illustrate that the NS-SAR ADC consumes 6.19 µW when operating at 1-MS/s. It achieves a Schreier FoM of 168.2 dB with 68.13 dB signal to noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) at an oversampling ratio (OSR) of 8 and 1 V supply in 180 nm CMOS process.

articleTitle: A Continuous-Time Readout IC with 0.12 aF/√Hz for Capacitive Inertial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-time integrated readout interface for inertial sensors with high energy efficiency and high resolution. A dual digital-to-analog conversion (dual DAC) scheme is proposed which reduces the large DC baseline capacitance while preserving a high gain in the capacitance-to-voltage converter (CVC). A continuous-time delta-sigma modulator (CTΔΣM) is used to digitize the output signal of the CVC without kT/C noise. This results in a precision capacitive readout IC with a 5.5aF resolution in 0.5ms conversion time. It consumes 1.8mW. An inertial sensing system, consisting of the readout IC and a MEMS inertial sensor, achieves a resolution of 17.02ng/√Hz.

articleTitle: A 4×25Gb/s De-Serializer with Baud-Rate Sampling CDR and Standing-Wave Clock Distribution for NIC Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 4 × 25Gb/s de-serializer using a baud-rate sampling clock and data recovery (BR-CDR) is presented for NIC optical interconnects. The integrating front-end (IFE) circuit is proposed to eliminate half of the sampling phases in the phase detector. The de-serializer employs a continuous-time linear equalizer, a phase-interpolation-based BR-CDR, and a source-series-terminated driver in each channel. The standing-wave distribution network delivers a low-jitter 12.5-GHz clock to all four channels across a 2-mm distance under low power consumption. Measurements show that the 4-channel de-serializer recovers 25-Gb/s inputs with significant inter-symbol interference, achieving a 1.2-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ppd</inf> output-swing with 3.43-ps RMS jitter, at the cost of 306-mW power.

articleTitle: 10kV 4H-SiC IGBT Based on the Multi-floating-zone Junction Terminal Extension(MFZ-JTE) Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The 10kV 4H-SiC p-IGBT with the multi-floating-zone junction terminal extension(MFZ-JTE) structure was demonstrated in this paper. According to the basic principle and simulation results of the device, the key parameters of the device are optimized, the layout and process flow are designed. The 10 kV 4H-SiC p-IGBTs have been prepared. The device shows a Maximum breakdown voltage of 12.5kV (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>=50.2nA@10kV) at Vg=0V.When the gate bias is -40 V and the conduction current density is 100 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the conductive voltage drop is 8.3 V, and the differential specific on-resistance is 38.9 mΩ•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Optical Phased Array with Reduced Phase Tuning Resolution
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper studies the minimum thermo-tuning resolution for calibrating and steering the 1-D optical phased array (OPA) through simulation and experiment. Through simulation, we determined the factors, including antenna pitch d, wavelength λ, and calibration procedure, that affect the phase tuning resolution requirement of 1-D OPAs. Simulation results show that the resolution can be reduced to 2 bits without degrading the beam quality. Furthermore, an OPA with 128 antennas is implemented. Experimental results validate that 2 bits resolution is sufficient to calibrate the 1-D OPA with the most power concentrated at the target direction.

articleTitle: A Ternary Memristive Logic-in-Memory Design for Fast Data Scan
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a set of ternary logic operations including MAX, NMAX, and XOR with memristive logic-in-memory for fast data scan. A ternary database column-scalar scan algorithm and a data-aware mapping method to map the ternary logic gates to crossbar arrays are also presented to achieve high execution parallelism with reduced code length and operation steps. Experiment result shows that the steps of data scan based on the proposed ternary logic-in-memory is reduced by up to 59.16% compared to the previous binary logic-in-memory designs.

articleTitle: A Dipole Antenna with 2-Stage Cross-Coupled Active RBR for 2.45 GHz Energy Harvesting Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: in this paper, a single PCB board integrated 2.45 GHz energy harvesting system is proposed, which contains a dipole antenna, a ring directional coupler, impedance matching network and a 2-stage cross-coupled active rectifier boost regulator (RBR) chip. FR-4 with dielectric constant of 4.6 and thickness of 1.6mm PCB board is adopted. The on-board dipole antenna with dual-band and high-gain is designed as rectenna to harvesting RF signal. The ring directional coupler is used to convert single-ended RF signal into differential signals with phase difference of 180 degrees. The impedance matching network is designed to match frequency of 2.45 GHz. A 2-stage cross-coupled active RBR chip is designed with standard 180nm CMOS process, and installed on the PCB board with chip-on-board (CoB) package. Measurement results show that when the output power of PA is 18 dBm@2.45 GHz and the distance between transmitting antenna and dipole antenna is 10 cm, the RBR output voltage of 3.88 V and 1.49 V under 10 MΩ and 5 KΩ load resistance are achieving, respectively.

articleTitle: LAEPS: LDPC LLR Adaptive Estimation Based on Pattern Set Distribution Variation in 3D Charge Trap NAND Flash Memories
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Low-density parity-check (LDPC) code with the soft decoding algorithm has been widely used in 3D NAND flash memories to improve the system reliability, because of its strong error correction ability. However, the accuracy of the soft information represented by the Log-Likelihood Ratios (LLRs) is an important factor which affects the error correction ability of the LDPC decoder. To improve the accuracy of LLRs, a novel LLR Adaptive Estimation scheme based on Pattern Set distribution variation (LAEPS) in 3D charge trap NAND flash memories is presented in this paper. LAEPS estimates the LLR based on not only the information proved by multi-read but also the information proved by adjacent cells in the same channel. Experimental results by silicon test illustrate that LAEPS increases the correction capability of LDPC soft decoding to 1.4x, and decreases the decoding iteration and RBER to about 0.7x and 0.8x.

articleTitle: A DC-4GHz High Linearity Attenuator with Negative Temperature Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In general, the gain of the RF transceiver system decreases as the temperature increases. This paper implements a high linearity attenuator whose attenuation decreases with increasing temperature on 0.13um SOI process, which can compensate the gain decrease of other modules in RF system. The operating frequency is DC-4GHz. It uses a voltage-controlled attenuator with a negative and linear temperature coefficient voltage, and the attenuation slope can be configured while maintaining the lowest attenuation at high temperature. The attenuation can reduce about 6dB from -40°C to 85°C, and the minimum attenuation at 85°C is maintained about 2.5dB. While the attenuator is dc-coupled to 0V, a large number of MOSFETs stacked are used to greatly improve the linearity. The measured IIP3 is about 50dBm, and the input 1dB compression is about 30dBm. The die size is 1580um*1680um.

articleTitle: A high throughput spatially coupled low density generator matrix coding system
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Spatially coupled low density generator matrix (SC- LDGM) code is a novel code proposed in recent years but not implemented in hardware platform yet. We designed a hardware architecture for the encoder and decoder of SC-LDGM code, and proposed an efficient storage scheme for the message passing within decoder. We have validated our design using Xilinx evaluation board and conducted a bit error rate simulation. Results shows that our design achieves a throughput of 1.6Gbps and net coding gain of 7.3dB at BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>.

Author Keywords: spatially coupled low density generator matrix code (SC-LDGM)

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of 860V SiC Trench MOSFET with Stripe and Rectangular Cells
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the SiC trench MOSFETs with stripe cells and rectangular cells are both designed and fabricated on the 6-inch SiC wafer. Preliminary measurements demonstrate that the fabricated SiC trench MOSFET with stripe cells and rectangular cells could achieve a breakdown voltage of 980V and 860 V at a drain leakage current of 4.5 μA, respectively. The one with rectangular cells shows a current density of 10 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at a drain voltage of 2 V, which has a 1.6 times larger drain current density compared with the other one with stripe cells.

articleTitle: The Effect of High Temperature Ion Implantation on the Performance of 1.2kV 4H-SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The impact of high temperature ion implantation on the electrical performances of 4H-SiC MOSFETs is investigated. The effect of single-step high temperature ion implantation in P-well, N+, P+ regions and that of three-step implantations are compared firstly. It is found that neither high temperature ion implantation of N+ nor P+ can obviously improve the ohmic contact characteristics. The variations in electrical parameters are analyzed, showing that three-step high temperature ion implantations have made contribution to the improvements of Vth and RDSON. Therefore, it is significant to improve the performance of SiC MOSFETs by using three-step high temperature ion implantations.

articleTitle: A Robust and Efficiency-Improving Design for Single-Stage Multiple-Output Receiver of Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Based on the regulated active rectifier with PWM control, a new single-stage multiple-output (SSMO) receiver of wireless power transfer (WPT) system is proposed. In the conventional dual-stage WPT receiver, rectifier and DC-DC converter are used to rectify the induced AC voltage and regulate the rectified DC voltage, respectively. Compared with that, the single-stage AC-DC converter structure is more competitive in minimizing the power loss and the chip area. In order to enhance the robustness of the system, a new phase-inversed multi-PWM control method and a detuned circuit with efficiency-improving property are developed to cope with the undesired problems caused by all branches being turned on or turned off at the same time. Simulation results prove that the maximum efficiency of the receiver is almost 82% at three output voltages of 1.2V, 1.8V, and 2.5V, respectively.

articleTitle: A Fast Method for Steady-State Memristor Crossbar Array Circuit Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work we propose an effective preconditioning technique to accelerate the steady-state simulation of large-scale memristor crossbar arrays (MCAs). We exploit the structural regularity of MCAs to develop a specially-crafted preconditioner that can be efficiently evaluated utilizing tensor products and block matrix inversion. Numerical experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique compared to mainstream preconditioners.

articleTitle: A novel high quantum efficiency SiGe Phototransistor detector
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: We report on a novel SiGe phototransistor with high quantum efficiency and high responsivity which is fabricated by a standard 0.35um BiCMOS process. The epitaxy structure, especially the base/emitter interface are designed carefully to ensure a good BE hetero-junction interface and high optical responsivity. The compounded base consisting of a P<sup>-</sup>Si layer and a P<sup>-</sup>SiGe layer is adopted to weak the serious effect coming from impurity diffusion during fabrication. The fabricated devices are measured at 1V of collector voltage and exhibit maximum responsivity exceeding 4.27A/W with a dark current of about 2.27x10<sup>-8</sup>A. When the incident optical power is 2.29uW, the collector current can reach 9.78uA at the collector voltage V<inf>CE</inf> of 1V. At the same time, the external quantum efficiency of the device can be calculated as high as 623%.

articleTitle: A High Accuracy & Low Power EDR Estimation Processor for Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, a high accuracy and low power ECG-derived respiratory (EDR) estimation processor has been proposed. Several techniques have been proposed to improve the accuracy with low computational complexity, including QRS detection using refractory period refreshing and adaptive threshold EDR estimation. Implemented using a 40nm process technology, the proposed processor achieves a low EDR estimation error of 0.73 while consuming only 97.3 nW. It is suitable for wearable flexible health monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Mobile Grabbing Robot with Target Detection Using Quadric Fitting
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The recognition and localization of targets, navigation, and mechanical control are key problems for indoor grabbing task. This paper designs a vision-based mobile grabbing robot with a wheeled chassis and a six-axis mechanical arm. The vision perception employs multiple sensors to accomplish different function modules. A two-dimension (2D) map is draw by a lidar and tag codes fixed on the roof is observed by a binocular stereovision to realize a vision-based SLAM. In robot control, the path planning algorithm and kinematics of the mechanical arm determine robot trajectory and grabbing action, respectively. Three-dimension (3D) points colored by an inbuilt camera are acquired by a Kinect v2. For grabbing shape-specified targets, we propose a novel target detection approach, which combines 2D image-based recognition with 3D refined segmentation by quadric fitting. Finally, the feasibility of the robot scheme and the high accuracy of the proposed target detection approach are verified by experiments. The results show that the error of positioning robot is 14.1 cm at the speed of 0.2 m/s and the error of positioning target is 0.53 cm.

articleTitle: A Dual-Loop Spread-Spectrum Clock Generator with Accurate Spread Ratio
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a spread-spectrum clock generator (SSCG) based on voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) direct modulation. An auxiliary frequency-locked loop has been employed to guarantee a stable and accurate spread ratio under the variations of process, voltage and temperature (PVT). Besides, the spread ratio can be programmed via different counting value in the auxiliary loop. Implemented in UMC 0.18-μm CMOS technology, the SSCG achieves a 9.97 dB reduction in the peak power spectrum with 0.5% spreading at 31.56 kHz modulation frequency. The die area of the SSCG is 0.42×0.45mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A fully digital mismatch calibration algorithm for Time-Interleaved ADCs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A ref.ADC based two-step calibration algorithm is proposed for the timing mismatch between channels of time-interleaved ADC (TIADC). Firstly, the difference between the output of ref.ADC and sub-ADC at the same sampling period is used to estimate the timing mismatch, and a high-order Taylor interpolation algorithm is adopted to compensate it; Secondly, a calibration technique based on statistical principle is adopted to estimate the bandwidth mismatch introduced by the ref.ADC, and it can be compensated by the same Taylor interpolation algorithm; The final calibrated output is the mux of the timing and bandwidth mismatch compensated output. Applied to a four-channel 1Gs/s, 12-bit TI-ADC system, the simulation results show that, when the input signal frequency is 130MHz, after calibration, the signal-to-noise distortion ratio (SNDR) is increased from 29.77dB to 73.96dB, and the spurious free dynamic range (SFDR) is increased from 32.02dB to 98.44dB.

articleTitle: A parametric model for a high speed heterogeneous current-steering digital-to-analog converter based on compiled Verilog-A and SPICE
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
