abstract: This paper proposes an innovative modeling methodology and design flow for a heterogeneous DAC based on Verilog-A and spice, in which the parametric model of both analog and digital parts can be configured to describe the ports width and the other variables of the mixed signal circuits which are derived from the measured datas. The model is further verified by a 4 Gb/s, 14-bit heterogeneous DAC, which shows a good fitting between measured and simulated results of a variety of parameters including: gain / bandwidth, spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) and effective number of bits (ENOB) with the input sample frequency range between 0.2 GHz and 1.5 GHz. The validation of the DAC model offers a much convenient system level simulation for heterogeneous integration and mixed signal microsystems.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Magnetic Strong Physical Unclonable Function
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the advent of the Internet of Things era, strong physical unclonable functions (PUFs) have been proven to be the most suitable cryptographic primitives for secure and reliable authentication, due to their large number of challenge-response pairs (CRPs). This paper presents a lightweight construction for extending a weak magnetic PUF to strong PUF by embedding Corrected Block Tiny Encryption Algorithm (XXTEA) and XOR obfuscation circuits. Experimental results indicate that proposed PUF significantly increases CRPs space and achieves high security. The use of enhanced encryption provides a strong resistance against the machine learning attacks. Comparing with the previous strong PUFs with Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA), the proposed PUF reduces area occupation up to 74.54% and 59.29%, respectively.

articleTitle: Handheld Wireless ECG Recording System Based on Printed Metal-Plate Electrodes for Personalized Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A handheld wireless electrocardiogram (ECG) recording system using metal-plate electrodes is designed and implemented in this paper. The system comprises a low noise and high input impedance analog front-end (AFE) chip KS1081 and Bluetooth low energy (BLE) Microcontroller Unit (MCU) nRF52832 with proposed bio-signal processing firmware. Particularly, a pair of coin-sized dry-contact electrodes manufactured on a standard printed circuit board (PCB) are integrated in this system that can monitor the weak ECG signal from human body skin conveniently and comfortably without using any electrolyte gel. The manufactured prototype system occupied size of only 1.5cm by 2.5cm (core circuit), providing adjust differential gain from 34dB to 57dB over a frequency range of 150 Hz, and consuming around 2mA at single supply voltage of 2V when on-node data processing and wireless communication are both active. Experimental results showed the high accurate ECG signal that comprised P-Q-R-S-T waveforms can be obtained effectively from human fingers using the printed metal-plate electrodes. The preliminary results demonstrated that the developed handheld wireless ECG system is highly suitable for wearable personalized healthcare applications.

articleTitle: A High Power-Added-Efficiency Ku-band Frequency Doubler in 28-nm CMOS for Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 20-40GHz frequency doubler was implemented in 28–nm CMOS technology for automotive radar applications. The frequency doubler consists of a push-push core, an injection-locked core and two balun transformer. The push-push topology with 3-bit digital power control achieves output power control especially when the output power is deteriorated in high temperature condition. Moreover, an insert-locked technique is adopted in the frequency doubler to improve output power by 13dB. The proposed injection-locked technique was implemented by adding adjustable LC resonator which can make up for frequency deviation. By combine these two topologies, this design achieves high conversion gain (CG) of 6.7dB, high fundamental suppression (FS) of 39.9dB and high power added efficiency (PAE) of 8.56%. The chip size is only 0.10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding PADs.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Area and Energy Efficient Hardware Accelerator of Five High-order Operators for Vision Sensor Based Robot Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a reconfigurable hardware accelerator design of five major high-order operators for vision sensor based robot systems. These five high-order operators include convolution, median filtering, Euclidean distance, vector inner-product and iToF, which are intensively used in robot vision algorithms. In this work, a reconfigurable hardware accelerator design method for multiple high-order operators is proposed. FPGA implementation results show that the proposed design has achieved area efficiency with 17.54% reduced LUTs and 44.02% reduced FFs against the baseline hardware design of the five high-order operators. Case studies of Laplace edge-detection and iToF benchmark demonstrate the energy efficiency of proposed design with 19.70% and 6.2% reduction in energy consumption, respectively.

articleTitle: A 28GHz Bi-direction Transceiver with Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a compact 28GHz CMOS bi-direction transceiver for 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation mobile network new radio (5G NR) communication system with temperature compensation. To compensate the temperature characteristics of amplifiers, a biasing circuit composed of a current reference and an 8-bit current type digital analog convertor (IDAC) is proposed to realize both high gain steering resolution and low gain variation. Both of the TX and RX gain are around 22dB. It realized less than 1dB transceiver gain variation between -40°C and 80°C. The saturation power is about 14.5dBm. The chip area for a single path transceiver with biasing circuit is only 0.34mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with 65nm CMOS process.

Author Keywords: 5th generation mobile network new radio (5G NR)

articleTitle: Bits Mapping in Triple-level-cell (TLC) Charge-trap (CT) 3D NAND Flash Memory and its Applications to IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Error bits distributions in Triple-level-cell (TLC) charge-trap (CT) 3D NAND flash memory chips are studied systematically in this work. It is found that, firstly, hard error bits exist without dependences on the data patterns; secondly, soft error bits can be observed when programming a certain data pattern, and the distributions are unique in each block; thirdly, random errors can be distinguished by using shift-read operations, which originates from the random telegraph noise in NAND string current. More importantly, by errors mapping technologies, memory chips’ fingerprints could be generated, which can be utilized to assure data security.

articleTitle: A Low-latency NoC Router Priority Scheme for BFS algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Breadth-first search (BFS) is one of the most common used graph traversal algorithms and a building block for various graph applications. Many studies have been done to accelerate BFS-based graphic algorithm on multi-core architecture that based on Network-on-Chip NoC. However, BFS is known to be an algorithm that is difficult to obtain better performance from parallelization. One of the most important indicators to measure performance of BFS on a multi-core architecture is the latency of the NoC. In order to reduce the on-chip network delay, this paper proposes a priority strategy based on the global hop count of the packet. Experimental results by simulation show that this strategy can reduce the average packet delay by up to 21%.

articleTitle: A C-band FMCW Radar Transmitter with a 22 dBm Output Power Series-stacking CMCD PA for Long-distance Detection in 180-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 4.1-to-4.5GHz FMCW radar transmitter suitable for long-distance detection using 180-nm CMOS process is introduced in this paper. The chirp signal generator is realized by an open-loop voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) with a 3-bit switching capacitor array and a distributed-bias varactor array, which guarantee the high linearity of the frequency tuning curves. A 2-series stacking current mode class-D (CMCD) power amplifier (PA) is proposed to achieve remarkable power transmission and efficiency. The measured phase noise from the highest frequency is -123.0_dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset, and the tuning linearity can be calibrated to less than 10%. The output power is more than 22dBm and the drain efficiency is more than 30% across the whole 4.1-to-4.5GHz. The proposed FMCW transmitter occupies 3mm×2.3mm die area, including testing pads.

articleTitle: Direct Cu-polyimide Bonding Achieved by Surface Activation and Pt-catalyzed Formic Acid Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Recent flexible printed circuit applications of high-frequency wireless communication systems require thicker metal layers on substrates for lower ohmic losses. In this paper, a Cu layer over 50-micron thick was directly generated on the polyimide substrate by heterogeneous bonding method without interlayer. The polyimide was first sputtered a 200 nm-thick Cu layer, and then was activated by oxygen plasma to improve its hydrophilicity and achieve direct adhesion between polyimide and nanoscale Cu deposition, and eventually was bonded with a 50micron-thick Cu foil in a Pt-catalyzed formic acid atmosphere by thermo-compression. The effectiveness of this method was verified by comparing bonding interfaces, shear strength, and fracture modes of bonded samples with and without a Cr interlayer. This method provides a new idea for the integration of heterogeneous materials needed in wearable products and flexible printed circuits.

articleTitle: Bonding Process Measurement System Analysis Based on Characteristic Parameter Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Traditional measurement system analysis method cannot be used in bonding process measurement system that is destructive and non-repeatable. A analysis method based on characteristic parameter simulation to select substitute sample is proposed in this paper. A linear statistical model is established which shows measurement result total variation includes simulation variation caused by random data generation and substitute sample simulation. Average and Range method is used to calculate bonding measurement system repeatability and reproducibility with standard weights. It is proved that measurement system analysis based on characteristic parameter simulation can reflect real measurement system variation and reduce analysis cost of manufacturer.

articleTitle: A 834 pW CMOS Voltage and Current Reference Working from 0°C to 120°C
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes a simple circuit of an ultra-low-power CMOS-based voltage and current reference for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. We proposed a temperature independent pseudo resistor array with high temperature curvature correction technique. This resistor array realizes V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REF</inf> and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REF</inf> with pico-watt level power consumption in a small area. The reference was designed using a standard 0.18-μm CMOS technology. And at room temperature, the total power consumption is only 834 pW. The simulated V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REF</inf> and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REF</inf> are 0.45 V and 39 pA, with the temperature coefficients of 93 ppm/°C and 345 ppm/°C from 0°C to 120°C, respectively.

articleTitle: A 1.1-V 26.2-ppm/°C Sub-Bandgap Voltage Reference with 6.5-nW Power Consumption Composed of Subthreshold CMOSs and Single BJT
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper illustrates a methodology to design an ultra-low power bandgap voltage reference with high accuracy to counteract the effect of temperature using single BJT and MOSFETs working in subthreshold region. The study provides a new insight into compensation of complementary-to-absolute-temperature(CTAT) with a nano-watt proportional-to-absolute-temperature(PTAT) voltage generator with process variation brought by threshold voltage reduced. Designed in a 180-nm CMOS process technology, the circuit has a measured 26.2-ppm/°C temperature coefficient under a wide range of -40°C~125°C and an overall 0.234% variation coefficient among 9 chips with an active area of 0.0264-mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The experimental result shows the voltage reference can operate with a supply voltage down to 1.1-V and a full frequency PSRR better than -35dB while the power consumption is only 6.435-nW.

articleTitle: Moiré-Based Nanoprecision Bonding Alignment System for Hybrid Integration
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Wafer bonding alignment is one of the most important manufacturing processes in 3D integration, especially in high-density interconnection. A nanoprecision alignment system based on moiré fringes suitable for both optical transparent or opaque advanced wafers is proposed and named MoiréView. Moiré fringes are sensitive to gratings superposition status and beneficial for improving the accuracy into the nanoscale. The alignment system, which contains optical part, mechanical handling part, and signal process part, is developed to align bonding wafers without transparency requirements. The alignment operation includes optical system calibration, wafer position recognition, and wafer alignment. Using the moiré-based alignment method, we believe the system developed has sufficient potential to be a versatile and efficient method for high-density new-generation 3D integration.

articleTitle: Compact Modeling and Analysis of a Typical Inter-Chiplet Serial High Speed Link on an Active Interposer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: High bit rate, high density, low power consumption, low voltage and high current are among the major features and demands of today’s high-speed serial link among ICs/chiplets mounted on an interposer. With the development of serial link subsystem towards higher throughput, the data transmission rate has increased significantly. The validation of the design for high-speed serial links concerning signal integrity and power integrity has brought great challenges to engineers at home and abroad. There is still plenty of room in the studies relating to process optimization, measurement/analysis and system design of TSV (through silicon via) enabled silicon interposer. Interconnect elements such as TSVs and RDLs (redistribution layer) present non-ideal factors that impact negatively on the signal integrity and power integrity of serial links among ICs on an active interposer. In this paper, we first introduce the passive interconnection composed of TSV/RDL and their equivalent circuit model. Then, we use a compact modeling method to simulate the whole high speed serial full-link, in order to reveal the behavior of the data transmission and signal quality. The modeling and simulation results for high-speed serial links per various PICe specs are revealed, based on commercial tools, such as ADS (Advanced Design System) software.

articleTitle: A 127 nA Quiescent Current Capacitorless NMOS LDO with Fast-Transient Response
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a fully-on-chip, NMOS low dropout (LDO) regulator with nA quiescent current is proposed. This work combines the dynamic and adaptive current biasing techniques to improve the transient response while maintaining the quiescent current at nA level. The proposed LDO is designed in a 0.18-μm CMOS process and consumes 127 nA quiescent current with 100 mV dropout voltage for generating an output voltage of 800 mV. Furthermore, the output voltage undershoots 215 mv and takes less than 400 ns settling time when the load current steps from 1 μA to 10 mA in 500 ns.

articleTitle: A 161mW 32Gb/s ADC-Based NRZ SerDes Receiver Front End in 28nm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 32-Gb/s NRZ ADC-based SerDes receiver front end is presented in TSMC 28nm process. The front end consists of a degenerated CML combined with Gm-TIA Continuous Time Equalizer (CTLE) which provides equalization, gain as well as buffering at 16GHz, followed by a 32-way time-interleaved Analog-to-Digital Converter (TI-ADC), which is implemented in a 4x8 hierarchy. The Gm-TIA structure is utilized as an active inductor, combined with neutralization capacitor, achieving required bandwidth without using passive inductor. The gain, offset and sample clock error calibrations are implemented. This proposed front end operates at 32Gb/s achieving SNR of 36.4dB and SFDR 46.25dB at lower frequency; 29.65dB and 41.52dB respectively at Nyquist, consuming 161mW combined.

articleTitle: Maximum Channel Temperature Estimation for GaN HEMT transistors with n-fingers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: a simple analytical model to calculate the maximum channel temperature in the AlGaN/ GaN HEMT transistor with a different number of gate fingers is presented. The analytical form of the model and its simplicity enable the model to be easily used in SPICE models. The simulation results were compared with numerical data from COMSOL, which indicates the advantages of the model to predicate the maximum temperature regardless of the number of fingers.

articleTitle: Using Word Line (WL) Interference to Reduce Refresh Operations on 3D NAND Flash System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As the storage density of 3D NAND flash memory increases, reliability issues have been the bottleneck. Among all reliability issues, decreased retention time is the dominant one. To extend the retention time, data refresh is a straightforward approach. However, refresh operations will introduce redundant operations, which hurt the performance of the 3D NAND flash system. With the observation that retention time can be extended by WL interference, this paper first proposes to extend retention time with WL interference practically, and then presents a refresh scheme, which refreshes only one-third of pages in a block and postpones the refresh operations on the remaining two-thirds of pages with WL interference. Finally, the evaluation results show that the refresh operations are reduced by 35.1% with 7-day refresh period. Compared with previous work, as a result of refresh reduction, the read and write response time are decreased by 34.2% and 46.5% respectively.

articleTitle: The effect of ultrasonic turn-on sequence for dual ultrasonicassisted soldering
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the mixed powder of 40%Zn+60%SAC0307 is used as the solder, and a new type of dual ultrasonic-assisted soldering process is used to successfully achieve the interconnection of copper and aluminum dissimilar materials. At the same time, a series of studies have been carried out on the effect of the ultrasonic turn-on sequence for dual ultrasonic-assisted soldering. By comparing the mechanical properties and microstructure of the joints obtained under different process conditions, it is concluded that the best process of dual ultrasonic-assisted soldering is to turn on two ultrasonics at the same time. The shear strength of the joints obtained by the best process can reach 28.45MPa, and the microstructures of the Cu/interface and Al/interface are relatively uniform, and the IMC layer is relatively smooth. There are two IMC layers at the Cu/interface, namely Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> (close to the Cu side) and CuZn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (close to the solder seam side), and a Sn-rich layer appears at the Al/interface.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Up-Conversion Mixer in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a Ka-band up-conversion mixer. It is designed and fabricated in 65-nm CMOS technology. The mixer comprises a double balanced Gilbert mixer and an active balun to interface the IF single-ended input with wideband IF and RF realization. It achieves 8.6 dB conversion gain with RF and IF frequencies spanning from 23.5 to 32 GHz and from 0.8 to 2.5 GHz respectively. The LO leakage suppression is 48 dB by calibration.

articleTitle: An Adaptively-controlled High-efficiency Buck Converter with Wide Dynamic Range for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a buck converter with high conversion efficiency and wide dynamic load range. The prototype has been implemented with 180 nm standard CMOS process, occupying a core area of 0.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The post-layout simulation shows the innovated adaptive control and low power techniques enable the conveter to achieve 96% peak efficiency with 10 nA to 10 mA (1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>) dynamic range, targeting on various kinds of Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Design of Polymer Bonding Scheme and its Application for Triboelectronic Nanogenerator Integration
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The way to improve the integration by reducing the chip size gradually approaches the limit because the size is getting smaller and smaller, and the three-dimensional chip is the best choice to continue Moore’s law. In this work, we proposed a three-layer 3D integrated structure based on poly propylene carbonate (PPC), and encapsulated the self-powered sensor based on tribo-electric nanogenerator (TENG) to detect the stress, vibration and other indicators in the structure. In order to assist this design, we also simulated the performance of three-layer structure based on PPC and contact separation TENG.

articleTitle: Measuring the fracture toughness of low-k thin films used in advanced packaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The low-k or ultra-low-k dielectric were implemented in interconnections of advanced chips to reduce RC delay. The fragile low-k materials are a significant risk to the packaging reliability, crack and propagation. In this study, we fabricated freestanding samples of low-k film by a film lift-off technique, and surveyed the fracture toughness of the thin film. To obtain the test samples, the lithography and micromachining techniques were used to pattern the film in designed shapes with and without pre-cracks and release them from the substrate. The samples were subjected to uniaxial tensile tests to measure their fracture toughness, as well as the Young’s modulus and strength. The test results showed that fracture toughness of the low-k film is about 1.33 MPa•m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>. The obtained properties of the low-k thin film can be applied in a finite element analysis of chip-packaging interaction (CPI).

articleTitle: A Compact 76-81 GHz Transceiver Front-End for Automotive Radar in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A compact frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) transceiver front-end for automotive radar application operating at 76-81 GHz is presented. The LO input frequency is multiplied by the push-push doubler twice to produce the millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) signal for mixing and transmitting. Two solutions about power division network of the low-noise amplifier (LNA) are discussed. The receiving signals which have been divided into two paths are converted into intermediate frequency (IF) by high-linearity passive mixers. Power amplifier (PA) with power matching optimization achieves sufficient output power and high efficiency. Fabricated in 40-nm CMOS, the transceiver front-end has achieved 10.76 dBm transmitting output power and 10.9 dB maximum receiving conversion gain at 77 GHz. The system consumes 60.2(TX)/72(RX) mW and the chip area is 4.32 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, including all pads.

articleTitle: A 100GBaud Optical Receiver Front-End in 90nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An optical receiver front-end circuit with low input noise for a 100GBaud optical link to support 100Gbps data rate on a single wavelength is reported. The optical receiver front-end is consisted of a transimpedance amplifier (TIA) , a main amplifier (MA) , and an improved output buffer (OB) . The optical receiver front-end circuit is designed in 90nm SiGe BiCMOS process, and can realize 67GHz bandwidth. The input-referred noise density is 11.34pA/√Hz. The transimpedance gain is 63.4dBΩ, the maximum maximum input current is 500uApp and the maximum differential output swing is 350mVpp. The receiver front-end circuit consumes 130mW.

articleTitle: A 2-GS/s 200-MHz BW Oversampling Continuous-Time Pipeline ADC with Adaptive Digital Filter in 28nm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An oversampling continuous-time (CT) pipeline ADC with RC delay line and inherent anti-aliasing is presented, avoiding aliasing from switched-capacitor circuit, high power consumption of buffer and excess anti-aliasing filter. The digital reconstruction filter is implemented using least mean square (LMS) engine, tracing the deviation of analog filter due to PVT variations and chip production. The analog segment is fabricated in 28nm CMOS, one CT pipeline stage clocked at 4GHz followed by a 13-bit 4× time-interleaved pipeline-SAR ADC clocked at 2GHz as the backend ADC. A Simulink model is established, and the 84dB SNDR @-2dBFS of 14-bit design specifications proves the rationality of the CT architecture and applicability of LMS engine in two pipeline stages clocked at respective frequencies.

articleTitle: Effect of conductive filament morphology on soft error of oxide based Resistive Random Access Memory
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The unpredictable soft-error is an important reliability issue hindering the application of the Resistive random-access memory (RRAM). In this paper, we investigated the influence of conductive filament (CF) morphology on the soft-error during the reprogrammable operation. Different filament morphology could be achieved by adopting different programing scheme for forming operation in the oxide RRAM with the structure of TiN/IL/TaOx /TiN. Hourglass shaped filament is more likely to be formed by using the bidirectional forming (Bi-F) scheme and shows more soft-error during the endurance measurement. The mechanism could be explained by the recombination of oxygen ions and oxygen vacancies in the active regions. This paper has guiding significance for the memory optimization and application.

articleTitle: An Analytical Model of Energy Band Considering Drain Doping Effect of TFET With Exponential Barrier
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An analytic model of the double-gate Si-based tunneling field effect transistor from source to drain is proposed. The Poisson equation is used to consider the effects of the source/drain depletion region and the charge in the channel. The energy band bending caused by doping concentration and the gate voltage modulation effect of different gate voltages are characterized. The model does not need to add additional fitting parameters, and can describe the concentration change and voltage change of the device. The model was verified and analyzed using Sentaurus TCAD, and the results were in good agreement.

articleTitle: Paper-based flexible broadband photodetectors functionalized by PbS quantum dots/Carbon nanotube networks hybrid structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Paper-based electronic devices have attracted much attention due to their excellent flexible and environmentally friendly properties. Here, we demonstrated a paper-based flexible photodetector, where PbS quantum dots contribute to a broadband photoresponse from the visible to the near infrared and metallic single-walled carbon nanotubes (m-SWCNTs) serve as interdigital electrodes instead of traditional metal electrodes. Our paper-based flexible photodetector exhibits a high responsivity of 70 mA/W and excellent mechanical stability after a thousand bending cycles.

articleTitle: Novel Selective Area Recessed Regrowth-free Ohmic Contacts to High Al-content Barrier
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, low resistance ohmic contacts to high Al-composition AlN barrier have been studied. Several different schemes: direct contact without recessed, selective area recessed ohmic contact with different dimensions, and the whole area recessed ohmic contact have been comprehensively compared. Surface roughness has been evaluated by atomic force microscope (AFM). The TLM results show a low specific contact resistivity of 4.2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> Ω•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> obtained using the Ti/Al/Ni/Au whole area recessed ohmic contact annealed at 840 ℃ for 60 s in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ambient. Ohmic contact mechanism for the different samples and optimum choice considering a trade-off between sheet resistance and contact resistance are proposed. These results are believed to boost the AlN barrier applied for high-frequency millimeter-wave fields.

articleTitle: Radiation Hardened Design of STT-MRAM with High Recoverability from Double Node Upset
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel radiation-hardened design based on spin transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) which can self-recover from any single event upset (SEU) case as well as double nodes upset (DNU). By using a spin transfer torque magnetic tunnel junction (STT-MTJ) compact model and a commercial 28nm CMOS design kit, the robustness of the presented design is verified by the simulation results, i.e., soft errors can be corrected at all sensitive nodes when the amount of the deposited charge (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">inj</inf>) reaches 60pC. There is an optimal balance of recovery time t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> and recovery energy E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> with the supply voltage around 0.73V, where the circuit has a small t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> of 1.489ns and a low E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> of 1.456pJ. As the size of the transistors and TMR of MTJs increase, the error rates (RER) of three cases DNU show a decreasing tendency. With W/L≥4 or TMR≥1.75, the recover error rate of all cases are reduced below 1%.

articleTitle: A calibration-free multi-phase sampling Type-II PLL
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a calibration-free multi-phase sampling Type-II PLL with a lowpass filter based multi-phase error cancellation scheme. The proposed technique enables the simulated reference spur to remain below -79.3dBc even with large multi-phase errors. Moreover, the proposed approach introduces an additional low-frequency right-half-plane zero, which increases the phase margin of the PLL. The design is realized in a 40-nm CMOS technology and verified with circuit simulation.

articleTitle: A 130-GBaud 2:1 Analog Multiplexer in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 130-Gbaud 2:1 analog multiplexer (AMUX) with four-level pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM-4) in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS process is presented. A number of ultra-high speed broadband techniques are used, which allow 130-Gbaud operation while consuming 1-W from a 3.3-V supply. The bandwidth is improved to 70-GHz by employing the degenerated resistance and capacitance in the emitter coupled logic (ECL) buffer.

articleTitle: A 47K Noise Temperature CMOS S-band LNA for Cryogenic Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage cascade low noise amplifier (LNA) implemented with a standard 180nm CMOS process for cryogenic applications. A T-type filter structure is adopted to expand the bandwidth. In addition, the characteristic of MOSFET at 77 K is proposed and considered. At 77 K, the LNA achieves a power gain of 18 dB with an input return loss better than 10 dB and a noise temperature of 47 K within a frequency range of 1.74 ~ 3.45 GHz. It consumes 9 mW under DC supply of 0.6-V at 77K.

articleTitle: An Ultra-low Power Consumption Dual-Output Subthreshold CMOS Voltage Reference
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A dual-output subthreshold CMOS voltage reference (CVR) with ultra-low power consumption and low temperature coefficient (TC) is presented in this paper. The first voltage reference (VR) employs a complementary-to-absolute-temperature (CTAT) voltage, produced by the NMOS with different threshold voltages, and a proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) voltage, implemented by NMOS with different aspect ratios. The second voltage is generated by a 3.3-V NMOS with a PTAT current. With a standard 0.18-μm CMOS process, the post-simulation shows two voltage references of 578.5 mV and 283.7 mV, with TCs of 31.47 ppm/°C and 16.73 ppm/°C, respectively, for a temperature range of -40°C to 125°C. The power supply ripple rejection (PSRR) of first VR are −72.5dB, −32.6dB, −39.9dB at 10Hz, 1kHz, 1MHz, respectively, and those of the second VR are −73.8dB, −34.5dB, −48.8dB at 10Hz, 1kHz, 1MHz, respectively. The consumed power is 30.5 nW at 27°C and 1.8-V supply voltage.

articleTitle: A 40 Gbps PAM-4 Receiver with 12-Tap Direct Decision Feedback Equalizer Employing 1.5-stage Slicers in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article describes a four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) receiver with an analog front end (AFE) and a 12-tap direct decision feedback equalizer (DFE). A 1.5-stage slicer is proposed and the layout arrangement is optimized to relax the stringent timing constraint of the first tap loop. The post simulation results show that, compared with the traditional strong-arm slicer, the proposed 1.5-stage slicer reduces the clock-to-Q delay by 18%, which allows the implementation of the receiver with energy efficiency of 4.2 pJ/bit at 40 Gbps and a core area of 0.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in 65-nm CMOS process.

articleTitle: A Highly Linear Multi-Clock Combining Phase Interpolator Insensitive to Interpolation Error
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel highly linear phase interpolator (PI) is proposed to effectively reduce the quantization error in a frac-N PLL without calibration. The multiple clock phases from a conventional PI are combined to generate one output clock phase with greatly reduced interpolation error. The multiple clocks advance or retreat by one VCO period while staying in a circular order and are subsequently combined to realize the desired fractional phases. A prototype 1/8 PI is designed. Simulations show that, with a +/-2pS initial interpolation error and VCO frequency of 5GHz, the proposed linear PI can reduce the quantization noise level by >16dB at both close-in and far-out frequency offsets. As comparison, under the same condition, a conventional PI worsens quantization noise at close-in frequency offset than that without PI.

articleTitle: A Time Domain Analytical Model for Lossy Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical model for time domain analysis of lossy transmission lines, which can be used for time domain analysis of lossy transmission lines. Dielectric loss, skin effect loss caused by signal trace and ground are taken into account. The time domain response results calculated by the model are in good agreement with measurement results, which proves the feasibility of using the model for time domain response analysis of lossy lines.

articleTitle: MIV Fault Modeling Method Based on Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Compared with integrated circuits based on through-silicon vias (TSVs), Monolithic three-dimensional integrated circuits (M3D ICs) have higher integration and relatively superior electrical performance. However, monolithic inter-tier vias (MIVs) inside M3D ICs are prone to failure. Accurate MIV fault models can provide the basis for subsequent fault detection work. In this paper, a MIV fault modeling method based on finite element analysis (FEA) is proposed, and MIV fault models are established by FEA softwares. The proposed method has high precision and is beneficial to further improve the detectable fault range of MIVs.

articleTitle: A 10-bit SAR ADC with adaptive VCO-based comparator for sensor chip
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 10-bit successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with adaptive Fig. 1. 10-bit SAR ADC with the proposed AVB comparator voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)-based comparator for sensor chip. The proposed adaptive VCO-based (AVB) comparator can improve the speed in large differential input, and reduce the power of the phase detector in small differential input. The simulation results show that the proposed SAR ADC achieves 57.68-dB SNDR and consumes 140 nW under a supply of 0.6-V at the Nyquist input rate, resulting in a Walden Figure-of-merit (FoM) with 11.1 fJ/conversion-step in a 180nm CMOS process.

articleTitle: An Accurate Analytical Model for Small Signal Behavior of MOSFET in Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An accurate analytical model of MOSFET without any fitting parameters is proposed which can work from DC-10f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>. The non-quasi-static (NQS) behavior is described by solving the continuity equation and drift-diffusion equation under small signal excitation, and the channel length modulation effect, the overlap capacitance and the junction capacitance are analytically modeled based on physical analysis. The proposed model is validated with the DC and small signal data of 180nm MOSFET which f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> is 100GHz obtained by TCAD simulations and it is in great agreement with the data up to 1THz.

articleTitle: A 0.0048mm2 0.43-to-1.0V 0.54-to-1.76GHz Bias-Current-Free PLL in 14nm FinFET CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes a compact analog PLL architecture for low-voltage clock generation systems. The digital PLL (DPLL) suffers from a large variation in the time resolution of a TDC over supply voltage. To achieve robust clock generation with a low supply voltage, a PLL without a charge pump (CP) is proposed for the design of a hybrid PLL. To verify the in-band noise performance of the analog CP-less PLL, a prototype integer-N PLL with a ring VCO is implemented in 14nm FinFET CMOS. The bias-current-free PLL features the compact area of 0.0048mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the minimum operation voltage of 0.43V, while consuming 1.27mW from a 0.6V supply at 1GHz output.

articleTitle: Lensfree on-chip digital holographic microscope with auto-focusing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Lensfree on-chip digital holographic microscope (LFOCDHM) is a simple and efficient miniaturized digital microscope with unique advantages of compact structure, large field-of-view (FOV), and high numerical aperture (NA) for point-of-care diagnostics. However, a compact and simple structure will increase the instability of an optical system that requires high precision. In practice, the distance between the sample plane and the detector plane is difficult to determine. Therefore, this paper proposes an LFOCDHM with an auto-focus algorithm to address the above challenge and studies the impact on the quality of final output images when there are certain deviations in the distance.

articleTitle: A Pseudo 943 million Frames Per Rate High-Speed Camera with Asynchronous Double-Frame Exposure for Motion Estimation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an asynchronous DFE (A-DFE) method which uses simple dual generic cameras with a dedicated designed hardware architecture for the camera mismatch, which significantly improves the upper limit of the measured velocity. Based on this method, we build up a pseudo-high-speed camera (PHSC) system for motion estimation on FPGA. The system achieves the shortest time interval of 1.06 ns, and the energy efficiency with 3.23 nJ/pixel on the low-cost XILINX Spartan-7 platform.

articleTitle: A 7-bit 1-GS/s Flash-SAR ADC with Time Interpolator in 45-nm SOI CMOS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 7-bit 1-GS/s flash-SAR ADC is presented. The ADC uses redundancy technique to eliminate the error caused by comparator offset and adopts interpolation technique to save power. Overall architecture and the principle of interpolation is introduced. The prototype is implemented in a foundry 45-nm SOI CMOS. Active area of the ADC is 0.026 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Post simulation results show that the SNDR is 36.5 dB and FoM is 49.8 fJ/conversion-step at Nyquist input.

articleTitle: A 1.65 mW 2.8 GHz Dual-Loops Class-C VCO Achieving 189 dBc/Hz FoM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A complementary Class-C VCO is presented in this paper in 65 nm CMOS process. Dual feedback loops and current-reuse technology are utilized to further power reduction. Multiple groups of varactors are used to improve the curve linearity compared with only one group of varactors. The simulation results show that it operates between 2.77 GHz and 2.98 GHz, achieving a 7.3% frequency tuning range. It has exhibited a phase noise of -122 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset and power consumption of 1.76 mW from the 2.87 GHz carrier frequency with a supply voltage of 1.2 V. The value of FoM is -188.7 dBc/Hz and the tuning linearity (KVCOmax / KVCOmin) is 1.10.

articleTitle: A Power Management Circuit for Dual Energy Sources Harvesting Self-Powered System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Aim to increase the output power of energy harvesting system for self-powered IoT applications, a power management circuit for dual energy sources including solar and impact-type piezoelectric energy, is proposed in this study. The proposed circuit can achieve not only the maximum power point tracking of each energy sources, but also the regulation of output voltage, thus, it can power a wireless sensor of IoT without extra power sources. The control algorithm of the dual-input power management circuit is realized by digital circuits to improve the flexibility and stability of the system. Finally, a dual energy sources harvesting system from solar and micro-wind energy is designed, and the control algorithm is implemented by a FPGA. The experiment results show the maximum output power of this system is 119 mW, and its output voltage can be regulated to 3 V.

articleTitle: A 150-170GHz 5-Bit Vector-Modulated Phase Shifter Based on X-type Phase Inverter Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 150-170GHz 5-bit vector-modulated phase shifter(VMPS) in 0.13-μm SiGe BiCMOS technology for D-band phased arrays. The X-type phase inverter(XPI) technique is adopted to change the phase of I/Q signal path and select output signal quadrants. Based on the proposed XPI technique, a VMPS architecture with compact area and low RMS phase error is proposed. The proposed VMPS achieves 11.25° phase step, < 2.43° RMS phase error and < 1.79 dB RMS gain error over 150-170GHz. The total power consumption is 37 mW and the core area of the phase shifter is only 0.27mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>

articleTitle: Analytical Delay Model in Near-Threshold Domain Considering Transition Time
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Near-threshold design faces the challenge of accurate modeling of timing behavior. Prior works define analytical cell delay models in near-threshold domain, but only focus on special cases of input transition time. An analytical delay model is proposed at near-threshold domain, which takes all cases of input transition time into consideration. The proposed model achieves satisfactory accuracy with the average (maximum) error less than 2% (6%). Compared with the competitive models, this work achieves at least 1.2X (6.2X) error reduction for ultra-fast (fast) input transition and satisfactory precision for slow input transition, which has never been modeled by prior works.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Thermal Matching between Multi-core Connector and Encapsulated Aluminum Shell
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Aluminum alloy has been widely used as the encapsulated shell in power modules because of its low density and high thermal conductivity. However, the thermal mismatch happened in the junction of aluminum shell and multi-core connector causes poor reliability of power modules. Focusing on the thermal matching between multi-core connector and encapsulated aluminum shell, we have analyzed air leakage phenomenon of power modules through thermodynamic simulation based on finite element method in this paper. Finally, a buffer ring structure is designed to significantly reduce the glasses’ stress of multi-core connector, which can effectively improve the reliability of power modules.

articleTitle: A 20~20 KHz Active Rectifier with Adaptive Delay Time Control and 1000X Frequency Detecting Techniques for Acoustic Wave Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a wide frequency range active rectifier for acoustic wave energy harvesting is proposed, which can operate in a frequency range of 20-20 KHz. The two PMOS switches are driving with cross-coupled connection, and the NOMS switches are designed as active-diodes. Adaptive delay time control technique as the loop control method is applied to regulate the conduction period time of the NMOS. In order to realize precise period time control under extremely frequency range, the gate signals (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GNA</inf>, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GNB</inf>) of the NMOS are generated mainly by switching the capacitor and the current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>), so that the NMOS can be turned on and off on time. The active rectifier is implementation by using standard 0.18 µm CMOS process. Simulated results show that its total power consumption is 13.5 µW at steady stage when the input frequency is 2 KHz and load resistance is 10 KΩ, the output power is up to 602 µW, and the PCE reaches 97.8%.
